title: Catch: a one-screen game
lead: Nothing in this job needs a search or a tuning. Write the whole game in one go from notes/how.md, then check it with a few runs that each read several ticks (--at).
brief: Build a small game called Catch. It has one screen.
- The field is 12 units wide and 16 units tall. A paddle 3 units wide sits on the bottom edge. It moves left and right at 8 units a second (keys: Left / Right, and A / D) and never leaves the field.

- Pieces 1 unit across fall from the top edge, one every 1.2 seconds, the first at the first tick. Each starts at a column chosen by a random source that is seeded by a number given when the game starts (`seed`, default 1). The same seed always gives the same game.
- Pieces fall at 4 units a second. After every 5 catches they fall 5% faster (4, 4.2, 4.41, ...).
- A piece that touches the paddle is caught: 10 points. A piece that reaches the bottom edge is missed. The third miss ends the run.
- The screen shows the score and the misses left. After the end it shows "Game over", the final score and how to restart (Enter). A restart begins a fresh run with the same seed.
- The game advances in fixed steps of 1/60 second. What happens never depends on how fast frames are drawn.
Someone who cannot play it by hand will check it, so the game must offer two things, however you build it:

1. A headless run: given a seed, a number of ticks and a script of inputs (at tick T: left, right, none or restart; an input holds until the next one), it runs that many ticks with no window and prints the state as one JSON object: {"tick" (the ticks run so far in this headless run: N after N ticks, whatever happened in them), "score", "misses", "over", "paddle_x" (the paddle's left edge), "fall_speed", "pieces": [{"x", "y"}]} (x from the left edge, y up from the bottom edge, both of the piece's centre).
2. A frame: after such a run, the view as it would be drawn, written as a PNG 480 pixels wide and 640 tall.
Hand in, in your work folder
- README.md: how to play it, the exact commands for the headless run and the frame, and what you checked yourself and how.

acceptance.text: The headless run exists, takes a seed, a tick count and an input script, and prints the state as the brief's JSON object.
The frame is written as a 480 x 640 PNG after a headless run.
Holding left for 200 ticks from the start leaves the paddle's left edge at 0; holding right leaves it at 9 (never outside the field).
The paddle moves 8 units a second: after 30 ticks of right from a known position it has moved 4 units (unless the edge stops it).
A piece appears at the first tick and then one every 72 ticks for as long as the run goes on (none after the end, until a restart).
Two headless runs with the same seed, ticks and script print identical states; another seed gives other piece columns.
A caught piece adds exactly 10 points and disappears; it is not also counted as a miss.
A piece that reaches the bottom edge away from the paddle adds one miss and no points.
After the third miss `over` is true, and further ticks change neither the score nor the misses nor the pieces.
After 5 catches `fall_speed` is 4.2 (5% more), and pieces move that much faster from then on.
A restart after the end begins a fresh run (score 0, no misses) whose pieces fall in the same columns as the first run's.
The frame of a run in play shows the paddle, the falling pieces at the places the state gives, the score and the misses left.
The frame after the end shows "Game over", the final score and how to restart.
README.md says how to play and gives commands for the two checks that work as written.
